explainer.heading: Weather vs climate
explainer.body: Weather is the condition of the atmosphere at a place for a short time (hours or days). Climate is the average weather pattern over many years.
explainer.example: 'It's raining in Bengaluru today' is weather; 'Bengaluru has pleasant summers' is climate.

explainer.heading: Elements of weather
explainer.body: Temperature, rainfall (precipitation), humidity (moisture in air), wind speed and direction, and air pressure together describe the weather.
explainer.example: A weather app shows 28°C, 70% humidity and winds from the west - those are weather elements.

explainer.heading: Measuring weather
explainer.body: Thermometers measure temperature, rain gauges measure rainfall, wind vanes show wind direction, anemometers measure wind speed, barometers measure air pressure and hygrometers measure humidity.
explainer.example: School weather stations often have a rain gauge and a wind vane on the roof.
explainer.hook: Baro = pressure, Anemo = wind, Hygro = wet.

explainer.heading: Why weather matters
explainer.body: Farmers, pilots, fishermen and planners rely on weather forecasts to decide sowing, flights, fishing trips and disaster warnings.
explainer.example: Fishermen are warned not to go to sea before a cyclone.
explainer.hook: Forecasts save crops, flights and lives.

questions.q: The condition of the atmosphere at a place for a short time is called:
questions.why: Weather is short-term; climate is the long-term average.

questions.q: Wind speed is measured with a:

questions.q: The amount of water vapour in the air is called ______.
questions.why: Humidity is measured with a hygrometer.

questions.q: Climate is the average weather of a place over many years.
questions.why: That is the definition of climate.

questions.q: 'Mumbai gets heavy rain every June to September.' This statement describes:
questions.why: It describes a long-term pattern, not one day.

questions.q: Give two ways in which weather forecasts help farmers.
questions.ans: Deciding when to sow or harvest; protecting crops before heavy rain, hail or frost; planning irrigation.
